stories.title: Are brain waves the next unlock for physical AI?
stories.simple_summary: Researchers are experimenting with using brain wave readings to help train physical AI robots. Instead of just showing a robot videos, they want to measure what a person's brain is doing while they perform tasks.
stories.why_it_matters: This is still early research that mostly matters to scientists and engineers — nothing you need to worry about right now.

stories.title: Making sense of the panic over Chinese AI
stories.simple_summary: A Chinese AI company released a smart assistant that caught the attention of American tech investors and made some nervous. People are debating whether Chinese AI is advancing faster than expected.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters mainly to investors and tech companies watching competition — it doesn't directly affect your daily life or business.

stories.title: Hugging Face CEO calls for ‘radical transparency’ after ‘unprecedented’ OpenAI hack
stories.simple_summary: Someone hacked into OpenAI's systems using an AI agent (a robot program that acts on its own), which is a new type of cyberattack. The leader of another AI company called for more transparency about what happened.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows AI systems can be vulnerable to attacks, but for most small business owners this is more of a warning sign to stay alert rather than an immediate threat.

stories.title: Monday.com is the latest tech company to blame AI for layoffs — here are 20 others
stories.simple_summary: Monday.com, a software company, laid off workers and blamed AI for making those jobs unnecessary. This is one of at least 20 big tech companies that have done the same this year.
stories.why_it_matters: If your business uses AI tools to replace jobs, this is a sign the technology is getting stronger — you should think carefully about how it fits into your plans.

stories.title: Librarians are hosting viral ‘Avoiding AI’ workshops for people who are fed up with Big Tech
stories.simple_summary: Libraries across the country are running workshops teaching people how to avoid using AI and stay away from it. These workshops are surprisingly popular.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're worried about AI, you're not alone — many people feel the same way and are looking for ways to live without it.

stories.title: One fallen power line exposed a growing AI data center problem. Here’s how to fix it.
stories.simple_summary: A power line went down in Virginia and caused problems for the giant computer buildings (data centers) that run AI systems. The problem shows these buildings aren't prepared for power problems.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters mainly to tech investors — if data centers fail, AI services go down, but this isn't something you need to act on.

stories.title: I tried out OpenAI’s new AI keypad — which will be fun for some coders and slightly mystifying to everyone else
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI released a new typing tool designed to work with AI in a special way. It's interesting to computer programmers but most people probably won't use it.
stories.why_it_matters: This is designed for professional coders — unless you write computer code, you can skip this news.

stories.title: Prentis, new AI lab co-founded by Reid Hoffman, Mark Pincus in talks to raise $100M
stories.simple_summary: A new AI company is raising $100 million and believes the next big use of AI will be automating routine computer tasks instead of writing code.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — it shows where money is flowing in AI, but no action needed for ordinary people right now.

stories.title: Midjourney bought the astrology app Co-Star
stories.simple_summary: Midjourney, an AI image company, bought an astrology app called Co-Star. The company is expanding from making pictures to offering horoscopes.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect you directly — it shows AI companies are trying new business ideas, but your horoscope app isn't changing unless you use Co-Star.

stories.title: Why Cognition bought Poke: AI personality is becoming a competitive advantage
stories.simple_summary: A company bought a smaller AI company partly because it had a friendly way of talking to people. They believe how an AI assistant sounds and acts is just as important as how smart it is.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use AI assistants, this means companies will focus more on making them easier and nicer to talk to — that's actually good news for users.

stories.title: You can’t ignore Google Zero anymore
stories.simple_summary: Google has changed how it works with websites — it's keeping more of the web traffic for itself instead of sending visitors to other sites like it used to. The old deal between Google and websites is breaking down.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a website or depend on Google sending you visitors, this could hurt your traffic — you may need to find new ways to reach customers.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Opus 5
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic released a new AI model called Opus 5 that is cheaper and less restricted than a previous version. It will probably be what most people choose to use.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Anthropic's AI tools, this is good news — cheaper and easier to use means better value for your business.
